note.text:
Solid–liquid mixtures:
• Decantation: let the solid settle, then gently pour off the liquid.
• Filtration: pour through filter paper in a funnel. The solid left on the paper is the residue; the liquid that passes through is the filtrate.
• Evaporation: heat a solution until the water has gone and the dissolved solid is left (salt from salt water).
• Crystallisation: heat the solution until it is strong, then let it cool slowly: crystals form (copper(II) sulfate).
• Simple distillation: boil the solution, cool the vapour in a condenser and collect the pure liquid (the distillate): pure water from salt water.

worked_example.problem: Ayuk wants drinking water from salt water and wants to keep the water, not the salt. Which method?
steps: Evaporation would lose the water into the air.
Simple distillation boils the water, then cools the steam in a condenser so it turns back into liquid water.
The salt stays behind in the flask.

cards.idea: Filtration: the solid stays on the filter paper (residue); the liquid passes through (filtrate).
Evaporation keeps the dissolved solid; distillation keeps the liquid too.
example: Salt water: evaporate to get salt; distil to get pure water.

cards.idea: Decantation: let the solid settle, then pour off the liquid gently.
example: Water from a bucket of muddy water left overnight.

check.prompt: In filtration, what is the filtrate?

right.text: the liquid that passes through the filter paper

wrong.text: the solid left on the filter paper

wrong.explain: The filtrate is the liquid that passes through.
Steam comes from distillation or evaporation, not filtration.

pick.t: water from settled sand in a bucket
pick.why: To separate water from settled sand in a bucket, use decantation.
To separate sand from muddy water, use filtration.
To separate salt from salt water, use evaporation.

pick.t: copper(II) sulfate crystals from its solution
pick.why: To separate copper(II) sulfate crystals from its solution, use crystallisation.
To separate pure water from salt water, use simple distillation.

questions.prompt: Which method would you use to get {x.t}?

misconceptions.explain: That method gives a different product. Do you want to keep the solid, the liquid, or both?

questions.prompt: Match each method with how it works.

pool.right: let the solid settle, then pour off the liquid
pass through filter paper: the solid stays (residue), the liquid passes (filtrate)
heat to drive off the liquid and keep the dissolved solid
heat to make a hot, strong solution, then let it cool to form crystals
boil the liquid and cool the vapour to collect the pure liquid

questions.prompt: Put the steps of simple distillation of salt water in order.

items.text: Heat the salt water in a flask until it boils.
Cold water around the condenser cools the steam into liquid water.
Pure water (the distillate) drips into a beaker; the salt stays in the flask.

questions.prompt: After filtering muddy water, which sentence is right?

right.text: The mud on the paper is the residue; the clear water is the filtrate.

wrong.explain: The filtrate is the liquid that passes through.

wrong.text: The clear water is the residue.
wrong.explain: The residue is the solid left on the paper.
Distillate is the liquid collected in distillation.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Distillation can give pure water from salt water.
Decantation pours off a liquid above a settled solid.

wrong.text: Filtration separates salt from salt water.
wrong.explain: Dissolved salt passes through the filter paper: use evaporation.

wrong.text: Evaporation lets you keep the water.
wrong.explain: Evaporation loses the water into the air: use distillation to keep it.
